usageNotes: Use this to remove a node from the Proxmox cluster configuration — typically after the node has already been shut down or when evicting a dead/unreachable node. The target node should be offline before removal; removing an active, healthy node without migrating its VMs/containers and storage first can leave workloads unmanageable. This operation returns null synchronously, but the underlying cluster config propagation (corosync quorum) takes effect immediately.

examples.summary: Remove a decommissioned node named 'pve-node3' from the cluster

destructiveReason: Permanently removes the node's membership from the cluster configuration; any VMs, storage mappings, or HA rules still assigned to the node become orphaned and must be manually reassigned or cleaned up.
tips: Migrate all VMs and containers off the node before removal — orphaned guests are not automatically reassigned.
Remove the node from any HA groups and storage replication jobs before deleting it from the cluster config.
After removal, the evicted node's local corosync/pmxcfs state is not automatically wiped — reinstall or manually clean it to prevent split-brain if the node is reused.
Requires quorum: if the cluster already lacks quorum, this call may fail or produce unexpected results.
